spec_match.rationale: Runs the exact migration ChromeStatus's interop_compat_risks names — code assuming a non-null styleSheet — against a live fixture whose imports include loaded, failed (wrong-MIME) and never-fetched conditional entries.

interactive.rationale: Two run buttons rebuild the fixture and execute the legacy and null-safe auditors for real, printing the genuine return value or the genuine TypeError text.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Blurb promises the compat story run live with both auditors over the same tree; that is precisely the page.

edge_cases.rationale: Fixture covers nested imports, a 200-but-text/plain failed load (no 4xx noise), and a parenthesized false-supports import; the states line exposes 141's wrong-fetch divergence explicitly.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5123480866783232 and the CSSOM interface.

conformance.rationale: The suite's failed-import-null and false-supports-null assertions pin the branch that makes the legacy auditor throw on 158; on 141 they fail honestly while the page shows why the legacy code appears to work.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CDP driver: both auditors returned 12 rules with states sheet,sheet,sheet — the documented pre-158 appears-to-work outcome, with the wrong-fetch divergence visible in the states line; console clean, no 4xx (wrong-MIME fixture), 0px overflow both classes. Partial: the TypeError path of the legacy auditor requires a nullable build and stays pinned by conformance.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts the null-safe auditor never throws (the migration contract) and records the legacy auditor's observed outcome per run.

design_system.rationale: Side-by-side result cards use shared tokens; threw/ok outcomes are rose/emerald on paper with text labels, not colour alone.

accessibility.rationale: Native buttons, pre blocks focusable (tabindex=0) for keyboard scroll, outcomes are text paragraphs, single polite output narrates each run including the import styleSheet states.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Result cards grid collapses to one column via auto-fit minmax(min(100%,20rem)); harness reports 0px overflow and clean console at both classes.

openQuestions.title: Show the legacy auditor actually throwing on Chrome 158
openQuestions.detail: On this 141 container both auditors return the same count (the silent-landmine outcome). On a nullable build the legacy card should flip to 'THREW — TypeError: Cannot read properties of null'; verify and consider screenshotting both worlds side by side in the page copy.

guidanceConsulted.query: two-column comparison cards that stack on mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, Xrem), 1fr)) collapses gracefully without media queries.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The legacy/null-safe comparison uses exactly that pattern (20rem basis), verified single-column at 360px with no overflow.

guidanceConsulted.query: announcing success and failure of a user-triggered code run
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Route the outcome through one polite live region; keep error text verbatim and visible, not colour-only.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each run updates the single polite output with the real return value or exception text; the outcome lines also carry explicit 'returned/THREW' prefixes.

summary: The interop-risk migration as a runnable comparison: legacy non-null-assuming traversal vs the null-safe form over a live import tree. Verified with the repo headless-Chromium-141 CDP driver (no chrome-devtools-mcp here): both return 12 rules on 141 (the silent pre-158 outcome) with the wrong-fetch divergence surfaced; the throwing path is pinned by the conformance suite until a 158 build can run it.
